meanings: (used to emphasize how good or bad something is)

components.note: 刂 (knife) — cutting, as in 到, 分, 刻; to cut apart means separate.
另 (lìng, other) — separating things into "other" parts: 别 is another, different, or "don't".
扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.

example.hanzi: 别提这件事了，我现在心情很不好。
example.pinyin: Bié tí zhè jiàn shì le, wǒ xiànzài xīnqíng hěn bù hǎo.
example.english: Don't even mention this — I'm in a bad mood right now.
example.fact: Psychologists have found that suppressing an unwanted thought, sometimes called the 'white bear problem' after a famous 1987 experiment, often backfires and makes the thought return more persistently than if a person had simply let it pass. This 'rebound effect' is one reason therapists frequently encourage acknowledging and naming difficult emotions rather than trying to avoid discussing them entirely.

examples.hanzi: 别提了，我今天又迟到了。
examples.pinyin: Biétí le, wǒ jīntiān yòu chídào le.
examples.english: Don't even mention it; I was late again today.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试题目很难，别提有多紧张了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì tímù hěn nán, biétí yǒu duō jǐnzhāng le.
examples.english: The exam questions were hard, and I can't tell you how nervous I was.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
午 (noon) — an old picture of a pestle or mallet, later borrowed for 'noon'. Memory aid: noon is when the sun stands straight overhead — 下午, 午饭.

example.hanzi: 会议安排在明天上午九点。
example.pinyin: Huìyì ānpái zài míngtiān shàngwǔ jiǔ diǎn.
example.english: The meeting is scheduled for nine oʼclock tomorrow morning.
example.fact: Human body temperature naturally reaches its daily low point in the early morning hours, typically between 4 and 6 a.m., before core temperature and alertness begin climbing as part of the circadian rhythm. This is one reason cognitive performance and reaction times tend to be measurably worse in the pre-dawn hours, a factor implicated in several major industrial accidents that occurred during overnight shifts.

examples.hanzi: 我上午有课，下午有空。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shàngwǔ yǒu kè, xiàwǔ yǒu kòng.
examples.english: I have class in the morning and am free in the afternoon.

examples.hanzi: 他每天上午都在办公室工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā měitiān shàngwǔ dōu zài bàngōngshì gōngzuò.
examples.english: He works at the office every morning.

components.note: 十 (ten) — complete and wide: 博 is broad, abundant.
尃 (fū) is a loose sound clue for bó; 尃 also in 搏 bó, 薄 báo and 缚 fù.

example.hanzi: 这座博物馆很大。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò bówùguǎn hěn dà.
example.english: This museum is very large.
example.fact: 博 means 'wide, abundant' and builds 博物馆 (museum, 'wide-things hall'), 博士 (doctorate holder) and 渊博 (erudite). 博客 is the borrowed word for 'blog', and 赌博 is gambling.

examples.hanzi: 他是一位博学的老师。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi bóxué de lǎoshī.
examples.english: He is a learned teacher.

examples.hanzi: 她正在读博士。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài dú bóshì.
examples.english: She is working on her doctorate.

components.note: 扌 (hand, 提手旁) — marks hand actions, as in 打 hit, 推 push, 拉 pull; 捅 is poking or jabbing.
甬 (yǒng) — close sound: 捅 tǒng. 甬 also sounds out 通 tōng, 勇 yǒng and 桶 tǒng.

example.hanzi: 他用棍子捅了捅鸟窝。
example.pinyin: Tā yòng gùnzi tǒng le tǒng niǎowō.
example.english: He poked the bird's nest with a stick.
example.fact: 捅 literally 'to poke', and a colourful figurative use is 捅马蜂窝 ('poke the hornets' nest'), meaning to stir up trouble. 捅娄子 means to cause a mess, and 捅破 'to puncture or reveal'.

examples.hanzi: 他捅了捅我,让我别说话。
examples.pinyin: Tā tǒng le tǒng wǒ, ràng wǒ bié shuōhuà.
examples.english: He nudged me to keep me quiet.

examples.hanzi: 小孩把窗纸捅了一个洞。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎohái bǎ chuāngzhǐ tǒng le yí ge dòng.
examples.english: The child poked a hole in the paper window.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.
阝 on the left is 阜 (mound) — as in 险, 阳, 阴: a walled yard.
完 (wán) is a close sound clue for yuàn; also in 玩 wán.

example.hanzi: 这座剧院能容纳两千名观众。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò jùyuàn néng róngnà liǎngqiān míng guānzhòng.
example.english: This theater can hold two thousand audience members.
example.fact: The ancient Greek Theatre of Epidaurus, built around 300 BC and seating up to 14,000 people, has such precise acoustics that a coin dropped or a match struck on its central stage can reportedly be heard clearly from the very top row. Acoustic researchers have found the limestone seating rows act as a natural acoustic filter, dampening low-frequency crowd noise while allowing higher-frequency sounds like speech to carry clearly.

examples.hanzi: 我们昨晚去剧院看了一场话剧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zuówǎn qù jùyuàn kàn le yì chǎng huàjù.
examples.english: We went to the theater last night to see a play.

examples.hanzi: 这家剧院的票很难买。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā jùyuàn de piào hěn nán mǎi.
examples.english: Tickets for this theater are hard to buy.

components.note: 卑 (bēi) — humble; as a part it sounds out 碑 bēi, 脾 pí and 牌 pái.
阝 (town, from 邑) on the right — marks places, as in 都, 邮, 邻; 鄙 was a remote town, hence rustic, mean.
啚 (tú) is only a loose hint for bǐ.

example.hanzi: 大家都觉得他的做法非常卑鄙。
example.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu juéde tā de zuòfǎ fēicháng bēibǐ.
example.english: Everyone felt his actions were extremely despicable.
example.fact: The word 'quisling,' meaning a traitor who collaborates with an occupying enemy, comes from Vidkun Quisling, the Norwegian politician who led a puppet government for Nazi Germany during World War II. Quisling was tried and executed for treason in 1945, and his name entered common usage as a byword for betrayal within just a few years of his collaboration becoming public.

examples.hanzi: 他用卑鄙的手段赢了比赛。
examples.pinyin: Tā yòng bēibǐ de shǒuduàn yíng le bǐsài.
examples.english: He won the game by despicable means.

examples.hanzi: 骗老人的钱是很卑鄙的行为。
examples.pinyin: Piàn lǎorén de qián shì hěn bēibǐ de xíngwéi.
examples.english: Cheating old people out of money is despicable behavior.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 怀 is to cherish something in the heart or bosom.
不 (bù) only stands in for the complicated sound part of traditional 懷 (huái); a loose clue.
心 (heart) — 心 marks thoughts and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感; 念 is to think of someone.
今 (jīn) — loose hint — 念 is niàn; 今 also sounds out 琴 qín and 含 hán, and means "now".

example.hanzi: 每次回到老家，他都会怀念童年的时光。
example.pinyin: Měi cì huí dào lǎojiā, tā dōu huì huáiniàn tóngnián de shíguāng.
example.english: Every time he returns to his hometown, he reminisces about his childhood.
example.fact: The 'Proust phenomenon,' named after the novelist Marcel Proust's famous madeleine-and-tea passage, describes how smells can trigger unusually vivid and emotional memories compared to other senses. Neuroscientists have found the olfactory system has a more direct neural pathway to the brain's memory and emotion centers, the hippocampus and amygdala, than sight or sound do, which may explain why a particular scent can suddenly transport someone back decades.

examples.hanzi: 我很怀念大学时的生活。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn huáiniàn dàxué shí de shēnghuó.
examples.english: I miss my life in college.

examples.hanzi: 出国以后，他常常怀念家乡的饭菜。
examples.pinyin: Chūguó yǐhòu, tā chángcháng huáiniàn jiāxiāng de fàncài.
examples.english: After going abroad, he often misses the food from home.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house, as in 家, 安, 室; 宽 is a roomy house, hence wide and generous.
心 (heart) — marks feelings, as in 想, 思, 意; 恕 is a forgiving heart.
如 (rú) is a loose hint for shù.

example.hanzi: 她最终选择了宽恕伤害过她的人。
example.pinyin: Tā zuìzhōng xuǎnzé le kuānshù shānghài guò tā de rén.
example.english: She eventually chose to forgive the person who had hurt her.
example.fact: South Africa's Truth and Reconciliation Commission, established in 1996 after the end of apartheid, offered perpetrators of politically motivated crimes amnesty in exchange for full public testimony about what they had done. Chaired by Archbishop Desmond Tutu, the commission was built on the idea that public acknowledgment of wrongdoing, rather than punishment alone, could help a divided nation move forward.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该学会宽恕别人的错误。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi xuéhuì kuānshù biéren de cuòwù.
examples.english: We should learn to forgive other people's mistakes.

examples.hanzi: 他请求妈妈宽恕他。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐngqiú māma kuānshù tā.
examples.english: He asked his mother to forgive him.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — cliffs and rocks, as in 厅 hall, 厚 thick: a spring flowing from a cliff.
泉 (spring) — water from the rock: the source (源 yuán adds 氵 later); 原 is source, origin.
木 (tree) — a tree with a mark at the base: the root, hence source, origin, and the measure word for books.

example.hanzi: 这条路原本是一条乡间小道。
example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù yuánběn shì yì tiáo xiāngjiān xiǎodào.
example.english: This road was originally a small country lane.
example.fact: Rome's Via Appia, begun in 312 BC, was originally built as a military road to move troops and supplies quickly to southern Italy, and sections of its original stone paving are still walkable today, over 2,300 years later. Roman road-building standards required layered foundations of sand, gravel, and fitted stone so durable that some Roman roads remained Europe's best routes for travel well into the 18th century.

examples.hanzi: 我原本打算今天去，结果下雨了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yuánběn dǎsuàn jīntiān qù, jiéguǒ xià yǔ le.
examples.english: I originally planned to go today, but it rained.

examples.hanzi: 这本书原本是写给孩子看的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū yuánběn shì xiě gěi háizi kàn de.
examples.english: This book was originally written for children.

meanings: to gain first-hand knowledge of sth

components.note: 见 (see) — a big eye on a person's legs 儿: a person looking. The same 见 is in 现 appear, 觉 sense, 视 look.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; knowing means being able to name.
只 (zhǐ) is a loose sound clue for shí; the part replaces 戠 in the traditional 識.

example.hanzi: 出国留学让他增长了不少见识。
example.pinyin: Chūguó liúxué ràng tā zēngzhǎng le bùshǎo jiànshi.
example.english: Studying abroad broadened his horizons considerably.
example.fact: Astronauts who view Earth from space often report a profound shift in perspective known as the 'overview effect,' first named by author Frank White in 1987 after interviewing dozens of spacefarers. Many describe a heightened sense of the planet's fragility and interconnectedness upon seeing it as a single, borderless sphere hanging in the void, a shift in worldview some report lasting for the rest of their lives.

examples.hanzi: 我想去国外见识一下不同的文化。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù guówài jiànshi yíxià bùtóng de wénhuà.
examples.english: I want to go abroad and experience different cultures.

examples.hanzi: 他是个有见识的人。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì ge yǒu jiànshi de rén.
examples.english: He's a person of knowledge and experience.

meanings: to carry level with both hands

components.note: 立 (to stand) — standing upright at the tip or end; also in 站 stand, 童 child.
耑 (duān) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 瑞 ruì.

example.hanzi: 服务员端来了一碗汤。
example.pinyin: Fúwùyuán duān lái le yì wǎn tāng.
example.english: The waiter brought over a bowl of soup.
example.fact: 端 as a verb is carrying a bowl or tray level with both hands, unlike 拿 (hold) or 提 (carry hanging). It is also the root of 端午 (Dragon Boat Festival) and 极端 (extreme), where it means 'end'.

examples.hanzi: 请端稳一点,别洒了。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng duān wěn yìdiǎn, bié sǎ le.
examples.english: Hold it steady so you don't spill.

examples.hanzi: 这条路的另一端是公园。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo lù de lìng yì duān shì gōngyuán.
examples.english: The other end of this road is a park.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 握 is to grasp, as in 握手 handshake.
屋 (wū) — near sound — 握 is wò; 屋 also sounds out 幄 wò.

example.hanzi: 他紧紧握住了我的手。
example.pinyin: Tā jǐnjǐn wò zhù le wǒ de shǒu.
example.english: He held my hand tightly.
example.fact: 握 is the verb in 握手 (shake hands) and 握拳 (clench a fist). 把握 is both 'to grasp' and 'confidence': 有把握 means 'to be sure of success'.

examples.hanzi: 他伸出右手,热情地和我握了握手。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēn chū yòushǒu, rèqíng de hé wǒ wò le wò shǒu.
examples.english: He stretched out his right hand and shook hands with me warmly.

examples.hanzi: 你要握紧方向盘。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào wò jǐn fāngxiàngpán.
examples.english: You need to grip the steering wheel tightly.

components.note: 斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 做: 作 is something a person does or makes.
乍 (zuò) gives the exact sound; 乍 also in 昨 zuó, 炸 zhà and 怎 zěn.
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.
力 (strength) — visible inside 为. Memory aid: putting strength 力 into doing something; 为 is 'to do, to act' and, in 因为, 为什么, 'because/for'.
為 (traditional) — often explained as a hand leading an elephant to work. 为 is a cursive simplification, so the picture is no longer visible.

example.hanzi: 他必须为自己的所作所为承担责任。
example.pinyin: Tā bìxū wèi zìjǐ de suǒzuòsuǒwéi chéngdān zérèn.
example.english: He must take responsibility for his own conduct.
example.fact: The Nuremberg trials of 1945–1946 established the legal precedent that individuals, including heads of state and military officers, could be held personally accountable for actions committed under orders, rejecting the defense that following superior orders absolves responsibility. This principle, later called the 'Nuremberg principle,' became a foundation of modern international criminal law and influenced the creation of the International Criminal Court decades later.

examples.hanzi: 我们不能原谅他的所作所为。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù néng yuánliàng tā de suǒzuòsuǒwéi.
examples.english: We can't forgive his conduct.

examples.hanzi: 大家会看到你的所作所为。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā huì kàn dào nǐ de suǒzuòsuǒwéi.
examples.english: Everyone will see what you do.

components.note: 贝 (cowrie) — a shell, once used as money. As a radical it marks money and value: 财 wealth, 货 goods, 买 buy, 费 cost.

example.hanzi: 海边有很多漂亮的贝壳。
example.pinyin: Hǎibiān yǒu hěn duō piàoliang de bèiké.
example.english: There are many beautiful shells at the seaside.
example.fact: Because shells were once money, 贝 is the radical for wealth: 财, 货, 买, 贵, 贫. 贝壳 means 'shell', and 宝贝 ('precious shell') is a term of endearment for a baby or darling.

examples.hanzi: 宝贝,该起床了!
examples.pinyin: Bǎobèi, gāi qǐchuáng le!
examples.english: Sweetie, time to get up!

examples.hanzi: 这里的海鲜有扇贝和螃蟹。
examples.pinyin: Zhèli de hǎixiān yǒu shànbèi hé pángxiè.
examples.english: The seafood here includes scallops and crab.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) on the right, as in 到, 别, 利; 创 first meant a cut wound and then to create.
仓 (cāng) — near sound — 创 is chuàng; 仓 also sounds out 抢 qiǎng and 枪 qiāng.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 这个广告的创意非常吸引人。
example.pinyin: Zhège guǎnggào de chuàngyì fēicháng xīyǐn rén.
example.english: The creativity of this advertisement is very appealing.
example.fact: The term 'brainstorming' was popularized by advertising executive Alex Osborn in his 1948 book 'Your Creative Power,' which argued groups generate more and better ideas when criticism is deferred until after idea generation. Later research has actually found individuals working alone and then pooling ideas often outperform traditional group brainstorming sessions, partly because people tend to hold back ideas in front of others, a phenomenon researchers call 'production blocking.'

examples.hanzi: 这个广告很有创意。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guǎnggào hěn yǒu chuàngyì.
examples.english: This advertisement is very creative.

examples.hanzi: 她的创意让大家眼前一亮。
examples.pinyin: Tā de chuàngyì ràng dàjiā yǎnqián yí liàng.
examples.english: Her idea made everyone's eyes light up.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and roles: 你, 他, 位; 代 is one person replacing another, then a generation.
弋 (yì) is only a loose hint; 代 itself sounds out 袋 dài and 贷 dài.
夫 (man) is written twice, side by side — one man standing in for another, i.e. 'to replace, on behalf of' (替我 for me).
日 (sun) — the dictionary calls it a sound part, but tì ≠ rì, so treat that as unproven. Memory aid: two men take turns under the sun.

example.hanzi: 现在很多工厂用机器人代替人工。
example.pinyin: Xiànzài hěn duō gōngchǎng yòng jīqìrén dàitì réngōng.
example.english: Nowadays many factories use robots to replace human labor.
example.fact: The word 'robot' first appeared in Karel Čapek's 1920 play 'R.U.R.,' short for 'Rossum's Universal Robots,' derived from the Czech word 'robota,' meaning forced labor or drudgery. Čapek's robots were biological rather than mechanical, and the play's plot — in which the robots eventually revolt against their human creators — helped establish a theme that has echoed through science fiction ever since.

examples.hanzi: 我想用蜂蜜代替糖。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yòng fēngmì dàitì táng.
examples.english: I'd like to use honey in place of sugar.

examples.hanzi: 今天老师生病了，由另一位老师代替他。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān lǎoshī shēngbìng le, yóu lìng yí wèi lǎoshī dàitì tā.
examples.english: The teacher is sick today, so another teacher is taking his place.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
士 (scholar, soldier) — usually read as an axe or weapon, so a warrior or gentleman (士兵, 博士). Memory aid: 士 has the longer bar on top, 土 (earth) on the bottom.

example.hanzi: 现场有不少社会知名人士出席了活动。
example.pinyin: Xiànchǎng yǒu bùshǎo shèhuì zhīmíng rénshì chūxí le huódòng.
example.english: Quite a few well-known public figures attended the event on site.
example.fact: Sociologist Daniel Boorstin coined the term 'celebrity' in its modern sense in his 1961 book 'The Image,' defining a celebrity as 'a person who is known for his well-knownness' rather than for any particular achievement. Boorstin argued mass media had created a new class of public figures whose fame was self-perpetuating, a critique many scholars say became even more relevant with the rise of social media decades later.

examples.hanzi: 会上有很多专业人士发言。
examples.pinyin: Huì shàng yǒu hěn duō zhuānyè rénshì fāyán.
examples.english: Many professionals spoke at the meeting.

examples.hanzi: 这位人士不愿透露姓名。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi rénshì bú yuàn tòulù xìngmíng.
examples.english: This person is unwilling to reveal his name.

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks liquids; 汁 is juice or sap, as in 汤 soup, 酒 liquor.
十 (shí) is only a loose sound clue for zhī.

example.hanzi: 我早上喜欢喝橙汁。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zǎoshang xǐhuan hē chéngzhī.
example.english: I like to drink orange juice in the morning.
example.fact: 汁 is the liquid pressed or cooked from food, as in 果汁 (fruit juice) and 肉汁 (gravy). Compared with 汤, which is broth, 汁 is a thicker or concentrated liquid.

examples.hanzi: 请给我一杯果汁。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì bēi guǒzhī.
examples.english: Please give me a glass of fruit juice.

examples.hanzi: 这道菜的汤汁很鲜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài de tāngzhī hěn xiān.
examples.english: The sauce in this dish is very tasty.

components.note: 干 (dry; do) — a forked pole or shield. It lends its sound to 肝 gān, 杆 gān, 赶 gǎn, 汗 hàn and 岸 àn.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 脆 is brittle, crisp.
危 (wēi) is a loose hint for cuì.

example.hanzi: 他干脆辞职去创业了。
example.pinyin: Tā gāncuì cízhí qù chuàngyè le.
example.english: He simply quit his job and started his own business.
example.fact: Studies of startup founders have found a surprisingly large share previously worked at just a handful of companies — PayPal's early employees and founders, for instance, went on to start or lead companies including Tesla, SpaceX, LinkedIn, and YouTube, a group often nicknamed the 'PayPal Mafia.' Researchers studying this pattern suggest working closely with other ambitious risk-takers early in a career strongly predicts later founding a company oneself.

examples.hanzi: 你干脆告诉他真相吧。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ gāncuì gàosu tā zhēnxiàng ba.
examples.english: You might as well just tell him the truth.

examples.hanzi: 他说话很干脆，从不拖泥带水。
examples.pinyin: Tā shuōhuà hěn gāncuì, cóng bù tuōnídàishuǐ.
examples.english: He speaks bluntly and never beats around the bush.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 脆 is brittle, crisp.
危 (wēi) is a loose hint for cuì.
弓 (bow) — marks bows and bending, as in 弯, 引, 张, 强; 弱 doubles the shape and pairs with 强 strong.

example.hanzi: 玻璃制品非常脆弱，运输时要格外小心。
example.pinyin: Bōli zhìpǐn fēicháng cuìruò, yùnshū shí yào géwài xiǎoxīn.
example.english: Glassware is very fragile, so extra care is needed during transport.
example.fact: Prince Rupert's drops, teardrop-shaped pieces of glass formed by dropping molten glass into cold water, can withstand a hammer blow to the bulbous end thanks to immense internal compressive stress from rapid cooling, yet shatter explosively into powder if the thin tail is so much as scratched. High-speed camera footage has shown the resulting fracture can travel through the glass at speeds exceeding 1,600 meters per second.

examples.hanzi: 小鸟的身体很脆弱。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎo niǎo de shēntǐ hěn cuìruò.
examples.english: A little bird's body is very fragile.

examples.hanzi: 她看起来很坚强，其实内心很脆弱。
examples.pinyin: Tā kàn qǐlai hěn jiānqiáng, qíshí nèixīn hěn cuìruò.
examples.english: She looks strong, but she's actually fragile inside.

components.note: 水 (water) — a picture of flowing water; as a radical it appears as 氵 on the left (海, 河) or 水 at the bottom (泉, 冰).
木 (tree) — trees and wood, as in 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table; the fruit hangs on the tree.
田 (field) here is the round fruit drawn on the tree. 果 also gives the sound for 课 kè and 颗 kē.

example.hanzi: 市场上卖的水果又新鲜又便宜。
example.pinyin: Shìchǎng shàng mài de shuǐguǒ yòu xīnxiān yòu piányi.
example.english: The fruit sold at the market is both fresh and cheap.
example.fact: Botanically speaking, a banana is classified as a berry, since it develops from a single flower with one ovary and has seeds embedded in its flesh, while a strawberry is technically not a true berry at all — its real fruits are the tiny seed-like specks on the outside. This mismatch between culinary and botanical definitions of 'fruit' and 'berry' trips up even experienced botany students.

examples.hanzi: 我每天都吃一点水果。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān dōu chī yìdiǎn shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: I eat some fruit every day.

examples.hanzi: 你想吃什么水果？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng chī shénme shuǐguǒ?
examples.english: What fruit would you like to eat?

meanings: this (referring to a shop, restaurant, or company)

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement and place, as in 道 way, 过 pass, 近 near; the radical hints at "here / this way". The 文 part is not a useful sound clue.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 这家餐厅的招牌菜是红烧肉。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiā cāntīng de zhāopái cài shì hóngshāo ròu.
example.english: This restaurant's signature dish is red-braised pork.
example.fact: Hongshaorou, or red-braised pork, is closely associated with Chairman Mao Zedong, who was said to be especially fond of the dish from his home province of Hunan, and several restaurants there still market versions as 'Mao's braised pork.' The dish's deep reddish color and glossy sheen typically come from caramelizing sugar until it turns a dark amber before the pork is added, a technique distinct from simply darkening the meat with soy sauce.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的服务很好。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de fúwù hěn hǎo.
examples.english: This shop's service is very good.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司明年要招聘新员工。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī míngnián yào zhāopìn xīn yuángōng.
examples.english: This company will recruit new employees next year.

components.note: 尺 (ruler) — the main part, as in 尺寸 size. Dictionary story: a place where measures are discussed (口), like a bureau; 局 also means 'game' as in 结局.
口 (mouth/box) — placed inside 尺. It represents talk or a space; Memory aid: a ruler fitted to a mouth means rules are discussed in an 'office'.
田 (field) — farmland, the village's fields.
土 (earth) — land; field + earth gives "village" and then the unit of distance. 里 is the sound part of 理 lǐ.

example.hanzi: 局里最近来了一位新局长。
example.pinyin: Jú lǐ zuìjìn lái le yí wèi xīn júzhǎng.
example.english: The bureau recently got a new director.
example.fact: The word 'bureaucracy' comes from the French 'bureau' (desk, office) combined with the Greek suffix '-kratia' (rule, power), coined in the mid-18th century to describe the growing power of desk-bound officials in the French state. Sociologist Max Weber later formalized the concept in the early 20th century, arguing that a bureaucracy's strength — clear hierarchy, written rules, and specialized roles — could just as easily become a weakness when it produced rigid, impersonal decision-making.

examples.hanzi: 他在局里工作了二十年。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài jú lǐ gōngzuò le èrshí nián.
examples.english: He has worked in the bureau for twenty years.

examples.hanzi: 局里明天开会，请大家准时参加。
examples.pinyin: Jú lǐ míngtiān kāihuì, qǐng dàjiā zhǔnshí cānjiā.
examples.english: The bureau has a meeting tomorrow; please attend on time.

components.note: 户 (door, household) — one half of a double door 門. As a radical it marks doors and rooms: 房 room, 所 place, 扇 fan.

example.hanzi: 这个小区住着两百多户人家。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiǎoqū zhù zhe liǎng bǎi duō hù rénjiā.
example.english: Over two hundred households live in this neighborhood.
example.fact: 户 counts households (一户人家) and builds 窗户 (window), 账户 (account) and 户口, the household registration system that ties residence to a place. Don't confuse 户 with 门, which is the general word for 'door'.

examples.hanzi: 他家是农户,种了很多水果。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiā shì nónghù, zhòng le hěn duō shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: His family is a farming household and grows lots of fruit.

examples.hanzi: 请关上窗户。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng guān shàng chuānghu.
examples.english: Please close the window.

components.note: 王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球, 现, 理: 玩 first meant to handle jade.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.
王 (jade) — jade and gems, as in 球, 现, 理: 玩 first meant to handle jade.
元 (yuán) is a close sound clue for wán; also in 完 wán and 院 yuàn.

example.hanzi: 他只是拿新手机玩玩,没打算认真研究。
example.pinyin: tā zhǐshì ná xīn shǒujī wánwán, méi dǎsuàn rènzhēn yánjiū.
example.english: He's just playing around with the new phone, not planning to seriously study it.
example.fact: The IBM Simon, released in 1994, is widely considered the first smartphone — it had a touchscreen, email, and even a calendar nearly 15 years before the iPhone. It weighed over half a kilogram and its battery lasted less than an hour of talk time.

examples.hanzi: 周末我们去公园玩玩吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù gōngyuán wánwan ba.
examples.english: Let's go to the park for some fun this weekend.

examples.hanzi: 没事的时候，他喜欢玩玩游戏。
examples.pinyin: Méi shì de shíhou, tā xǐhuan wánwan yóuxì.
examples.english: When he has nothing to do, he likes to play around with games.

components.note: 争 (contend) — simplified from 爭, two hands pulling at the same object. See 战争 war and 竞争 compete.
雨 (rain) — the top part. Not about weather here: 霸 first meant pale moonlight and was later borrowed for 'tyrant, overlord' (霸道, 称霸).
革 (leather, to reform) and 月 (moon/flesh) form the lower part. Memory aid: an overlord rules above the rain, with leather armour (革) and the moon (月) beneath.

example.hanzi: 两家科技巨头正在人工智能领域争霸。
example.pinyin: liǎng jiā kējì jùtóu zhèngzài réngōng zhìnéng lǐngyù zhēngbà.
example.english: The two tech giants are contending for dominance in the field of artificial intelligence.
example.fact: Invasive Argentine ant colonies along the Mediterranean coast have merged across huge stretches of territory into a single 'supercolony' spanning thousands of kilometers, eliminating rival colonies in their struggle for dominance. Scientists consider it one of the largest cooperative units ever documented in the animal kingdom.

examples.hanzi: 各大品牌都想在市场上争霸。
examples.pinyin: Gè dà pǐnpái dōu xiǎng zài shìchǎng shàng zhēngbà.
examples.english: All the major brands want to dominate the market.

examples.hanzi: 这两支球队在联赛里争霸多年。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng zhī qiúduì zài liánsài lǐ zhēngbà duō nián.
examples.english: These two teams have competed for supremacy in the league for years.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 他, 做; 侵 is to encroach, as in 入侵; the right side also sounds out 浸 jìn.
犭 (beast, form of 犬 dog) — animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 狼 wolf; 犯 is to attack or violate, hence offend.

example.hanzi: 未经许可复制别人的作品属于侵犯版权。
example.pinyin: wèijīng xǔkě fùzhì biérén de zuòpǐn shǔyú qīnfàn bǎnquán.
example.english: Copying someone else's work without permission constitutes copyright infringement.
example.fact: The Berne Convention of 1886 was the first international agreement to protect authors' rights across borders, and it still underpins copyright law in more than 180 countries today. It introduced the principle that copyright exists automatically the moment a work is created, without needing registration.

examples.hanzi: 别人的隐私不能随便侵犯。
examples.pinyin: Biéren de yǐnsī bù néng suíbiàn qīnfàn.
examples.english: Other people's privacy can't be violated casually.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司被指控侵犯了他人的专利。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī bèi zhǐkòng qīnfàn le tārén de zhuānlì.
examples.english: This company was accused of infringing on someone else's patent.

components.note: 一 (one) — a single horizontal stroke is the number one; 二 and 三 just add strokes, so the first three numbers are tally marks.
白 (bái) hints at the sound: 百 bǎi is close, and 白 also gives 拍 pāi and 伯 bó.
萬 (traditional ten thousand) — 万 is the simplified form of 萬, which pictured a scorpion borrowed for the number 10,000; 万 also sounds out 迈 mài.

example.hanzi: 这座桥的建造花费了超过一百万美元。
example.pinyin: zhè zuò qiáo de jiànzào huāfèi le chāoguò yībǎiwàn měiyuán.
example.english: Building this bridge cost more than one million dollars.
example.fact: The Golden Gate Bridge, completed in 1937, cost about $35 million to build — equivalent to well over a billion dollars today — and its total length of cable wire, if unwound, would circle the earth more than three times.

examples.hanzi: 这座城市有一百万人口。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yǒu yì bǎi wàn rénkǒu.
examples.english: This city has a population of one million.

examples.hanzi: 他中了一百万的大奖。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhòng le yìbǎiwàn de dàjiǎng.
examples.english: He won a prize of one million.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
心 (heart) — mind and feelings, as in 想, 思, 感: 意 is what one has in mind.
音 (yīn, sound) is a loose sound clue for yì; 意 itself gives 忆 yì and 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 我无意打扰你,只是想确认一下时间。
example.pinyin: wǒ wúyì dǎrǎo nǐ, zhǐshì xiǎng quèrèn yīxià shíjiān.
example.english: I didn't mean to disturb you; I just wanted to confirm the time.
example.fact: Penicillin, one of the most important medical discoveries in history, was found completely by accident in 1928 when Alexander Fleming noticed mold had killed bacteria in a petri dish he'd left uncovered. He almost discarded the dish before noticing the unusual clearing around the mold.

examples.hanzi: 我无意中听到了他们的谈话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ wúyì zhōng tīng dào le tāmen de tánhuà.
examples.english: I overheard their conversation by accident.

examples.hanzi: 他对这份工作无意，打算换一个。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhè fèn gōngzuò wúyì, dǎsuàn huàn yí ge.
examples.english: He has no interest in this job and plans to change it.

components.note: 幸 (luck) — often read as an old picture of shackles; 'luck' is escaping punishment. The dictionary story (one alive 土, one dead 干) is a memory aid.
土 (earth) — the top. Memory aid: the one standing on solid ground 土 is the lucky one — 幸运, 幸福.

example.hanzi: 幸好你及时赶到了。
example.pinyin: Xìnghǎo nǐ jíshí gǎndào le.
example.english: Luckily you arrived in time.
example.fact: 幸 gives 幸好 and 幸亏 ('fortunately'), 幸福 (happiness) and 不幸 (unfortunate). In a polite formal greeting, 幸会 is 'pleased to meet you', a phrase heard at business introductions.

examples.hanzi: 我很幸运,考试通过了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xìngyùn, kǎoshì tōngguò le.
examples.english: I'm lucky; I passed the exam.

examples.hanzi: 祝你们生活幸福!
examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐmen shēnghuó xìngfú!
examples.english: Wishing you a happy life!

components.note: 氵 (water) — marks water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 温 is warm, like lukewarm water.
昷 (wēn) gives the sound exactly: 温 wēn, also in 瘟 wēn.
日 (sun) — marks light and warmth, as in 晴, 暗, 暖; 暖 is sunny warmth.
爰 (yuán) is a loose hint for nuǎn; 缓 huǎn and 援 yuán share it.

example.hanzi: 壁炉让整个房间变得温暖起来。
example.pinyin: bìlú ràng zhěnggè fángjiān biàn de wēnnuǎn qǐlái.
example.english: The fireplace made the whole room warm.
example.fact: The Gulf Stream carries roughly 30 times more water than all the world's rivers combined, moving warm water from the Gulf of Mexico up toward Northern Europe. It's a major reason London stays milder in winter than cities at similar latitudes in Canada.

examples.hanzi: 今天天气很温暖，适合出去走走。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān tiānqì hěn wēnnuǎn, shìhé chūqù zǒuzou.
examples.english: The weather is warm today, perfect for going out.

examples.hanzi: 她的话让我心里很温暖。
examples.pinyin: Tā de huà ràng wǒ xīnlǐ hěn wēnnuǎn.
examples.english: Her words warmed my heart.

components.note: 王 (jade, 玉旁) — marks jade and gems, as in 球, 玩, 理; 珠 is a pearl or bead.
朱 (zhū) gives the sound exactly: 珠 zhū, also in 株 zhū and 蛛 zhū.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 安, 室.
玉 (jade) — jade kept under a roof: treasure. The traditional 寶 also had 贝 (cowrie, money).

example.hanzi: 她把祖母留下的珠宝锁进了保险箱。
example.pinyin: tā bǎ zǔmǔ liú xià de zhūbǎo suǒ jìn le bǎoxiǎnxiāng.
example.english: She locked the jewelry her grandmother left behind into the safe.
example.fact: The Hope Diamond, one of the most famous jewels in the world, is believed to have originated from the Kollur Mine in India and is now valued at over $250 million. Its deep blue color comes from trace amounts of boron atoms in its crystal structure.

examples.hanzi: 这家店专门卖手工珠宝。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn zhuānmén mài shǒugōng zhūbǎo.
examples.english: This shop specializes in handmade jewelry.

examples.hanzi: 她喜欢戴漂亮的珠宝。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan dài piàoliang de zhūbǎo.
examples.english: She likes wearing beautiful jewelry.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.

example.hanzi: 每次提起那次旅行,他都会笑出来。
example.pinyin: měi cì tíqǐ nà cì lǚxíng, tā dōu huì xiào chūlái.
example.english: Every time that trip comes up, he laughs.
example.fact: Smell-triggered memories are so vivid they have their own name, the 'Proust phenomenon,' because the brain's olfactory bulb connects almost directly to the memory and emotion centers. Studies have found that scent-cued memories feel more emotionally intense than the same memories cued by words or pictures.

examples.hanzi: 老师没有提起我昨天迟到的事。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī méiyǒu tíqǐ wǒ zuótiān chídào de shì.
examples.english: The teacher didn't mention that I was late yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 他一提起家乡，眼睛就亮了。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì tíqǐ jiāxiāng, yǎnjing jiù liàng le.
examples.english: The moment he mentions his hometown, his eyes light up.

meanings: variant of 大夥|大伙[da4 huo3]

components.note: 大 (big) — a front-facing person with arms and legs spread wide: big. As radical, 大 is in 天 sky, 太 too much, 夫 man.
亻 (person) — people, as in 你, 他, 们: 伙 is a companion.
火 (huǒ, fire) gives the exact sound; 火 also means fire.

example.hanzi: 周末大伙一起去海边野餐吧。
example.pinyin: zhōumò dàhuǒ yīqǐ qù hǎibiān yěcān ba.
example.english: Let's all go to the beach for a picnic together this weekend.
example.fact: Emperor penguins survive Antarctic winters by huddling together in groups of thousands, constantly rotating positions so no single bird stays on the frigid outer edge too long. This collective strategy can raise the temperature at the center of the huddle to nearly 37°C even when it's -40°C outside.

examples.hanzi: 大伙儿别站着，快坐下吧。
examples.pinyin: Dàhuǒr bié zhàn zhe, kuài zuòxià ba.
examples.english: Everyone, don't stand around; sit down.

examples.hanzi: 大伙都同意这个方案。
examples.pinyin: Dàhuǒ dōu tóngyì zhège fāng'àn.
examples.english: Everyone agrees with this plan.

components.note: Four mouths 口 (vessels) with a dog 犬 guarding them — the traditional explanation; 器 is any vessel or tool, as in 武器 and 机器.
宀 (roof) — a public building where officials work; 官 is an official.
官 (guān) gives the sound of 管 guǎn, 馆 guǎn and 棺 guān.

example.hanzi: 心脏是人体最重要的器官之一。
example.pinyin: xīnzàng shì rén tǐ zuì zhòngyào de qìguān zhī yī.
example.english: The heart is one of the most important organs in the human body.
example.fact: The human liver is the only internal organ that can regrow to nearly its full size after part of it is removed — even after losing up to 70%, it can regenerate within a few months. This regenerative ability is what makes living-donor liver transplants possible.

examples.hanzi: 肝是人体重要的器官。
examples.pinyin: Gān shì réntǐ zhòngyào de qìguān.
examples.english: The liver is an important organ of the human body.

examples.hanzi: 医生说他需要移植一个器官。
examples.pinyin: Yīshēng shuō tā xūyào yízhí yí ge qìguān.
examples.english: The doctor said he needs an organ transplant.

components.note: 凵 (open pit) — oldest form shows a foot stepping out of a pit or cave: to go out, come out.
片 (slice, plank) — marks flat pieces and wooden boards, as in 牌 sign; 版 is a printing block.
反 (fǎn) hints at the sound: 版 bǎn is close, as in 板 bǎn and 饭 fàn.

example.hanzi: 这本小说去年正式出版。
example.pinyin: zhè běn xiǎoshuō qùnián zhèngshì chūbǎn.
example.english: This novel was officially published last year.
example.fact: Johannes Gutenberg's movable-type printing press, introduced around 1440, sparked a mass-publishing revolution in Europe — within 50 years, over 20 million books had been printed, more than all European scribes had produced by hand in the previous thousand years combined.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司专门出版儿童书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhuānmén chūbǎn értóng shū.
examples.english: This company specializes in publishing children's books.

examples.hanzi: 他的第一本诗集下个月出版。
examples.pinyin: Tā de dì yī běn shījí xià ge yuè chūbǎn.
examples.english: His first poetry collection will be published next month.

components.note: 刀 (knife, written 刂 on the right) — cutting, as in 分 divide, 刻 carve, 到 arrive.
七 (qī) is a close sound clue for qiē/qiè.
斤 (axe) — 斤 is an axe, as in 新, 析; 断 is to cut through, shown by the axe and threads cut.

example.hanzi: 暴风雪切断了整个村庄的电力供应。
example.pinyin: bàofēngxuě qiēduàn le zhěnggè cūnzhuāng de diànlì gōngyìng.
example.english: The blizzard cut off the entire village's power supply.
example.fact: In 2003, a single software bug in an Ohio power plant's alarm system helped trigger the Northeast Blackout, cutting off electricity to 55 million people across the US and Canada for up to two days. It remains one of the largest blackouts in history.

examples.hanzi: 请先切断电源再修理。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān qiēduàn diànyuán zài xiūlǐ.
examples.english: Please cut off the power before repairing it.

examples.hanzi: 他把绳子切断了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ shéngzi qiēduàn le.
examples.english: He cut the rope in two.

components.note: 王 (jade, 玉旁) — marks jade and gems, as in 球, 珠, 理; 玫 was a red gem, now part of 玫瑰 rose.
攵 (strike) hints at the sound méi, as in 枚 méi.
王 (jade, 玉旁) — marks jade and gems, as in 球, 珠, 玫; 瑰 is a gem, now part of 玫瑰 rose.
鬼 (guǐ) hints at the sound: 瑰 guī is close, as in 魁 kuí and 愧 kuì.

example.hanzi: 他送了她一束红玫瑰。
example.pinyin: tā sòng le tā yī shù hóng méiguī.
example.english: He gave her a bouquet of red roses.
example.fact: Roses are among the oldest cultivated flowers on Earth — fossil evidence suggests wild roses existed 35 million years ago, and archaeologists have found rose motifs in Egyptian tombs, pointing to cultivation stretching back thousands of years.

examples.hanzi: 园子里开满了红玫瑰。
examples.pinyin: Yuánzi lǐ kāi mǎn le hóng méiguī.
examples.english: The garden is full of red roses.

examples.hanzi: 情人节那天，花店里的玫瑰卖得特别快。
examples.pinyin: Qíngrénjié nà tiān, huādiàn lǐ de méiguī mài de tèbié kuài.
examples.english: On Valentine's Day, the roses sell especially fast at the flower shop.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢: to ask or discuss.

example.hanzi: 我讨厌下雨天。
example.pinyin: Wǒ tǎoyàn xià yǔ tiān.
example.english: I hate rainy days.
example.fact: 讨 literally 'to ask for' underlies 讨论 (discuss), 讨价还价 (haggle), 讨饭 (beg) and 讨厌, 'to dislike', literally 'to invite disgust'. 讨人喜欢 describes someone who is easy to like.

examples.hanzi: 我们在会议上讨论了这个计划。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài huìyì shang tǎolùn le zhège jìhuà.
examples.english: We discussed this plan at the meeting.

examples.hanzi: 她很会讨价还价。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn huì tǎojiàhuánjià.
examples.english: She is good at bargaining.

components.note: 山 (mountain) — marks hills and heights, as in 岛, 峰, 岸; 崇 is lofty, then esteemed.
宗 (zōng) is a loose hint for chóng; 综 zōng and 踪 zōng share it.
手 (hand) — two hands joined in respect: bowing and saluting; compare 扌 in 拿 and 打.

example.hanzi: 很多孩子从小就崇拜自己的父亲。
example.pinyin: hěn duō háizi cóngxiǎo jiù chóngbài zìjǐ de fùqīn.
example.english: Many children have worshipped their fathers since they were young.
example.fact: Ancient Egyptians worshipped the sun god Ra as one of their most powerful deities, believing he sailed across the sky each day in a solar barge and battled the serpent Apep every night to be reborn at dawn. Sun worship even influenced the alignment of monuments like the pyramids.

examples.hanzi: 我很崇拜我的老师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn chóngbài wǒ de lǎoshī.
examples.english: I really admire my teacher.

examples.hanzi: 年轻人常常崇拜歌星。
examples.pinyin: Niánqīngrén chángcháng chóngbài gēxīng.
examples.english: Young people often idolize singers.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — the right-hand side. Usually about cutting (到, 别, 利), but not in 前: it is a later corruption of the old picture.
舟 (boat) — hidden in the old form: a foot on a boat moving ahead, so 'in front, forward'. Usual explanation, though the modern shape hides it.
女 (woman) — women and family, as in 妈, 她, 姐; oldest form shows a hand arranging a woman's hair, a wife.

example.hanzi: 他和前妻仍然保持着朋友关系。
example.pinyin: tā hé qiánqī réngrán bǎochí zhe péngyǒu guānxì.
example.english: He and his ex-wife still remain friends.
example.fact: Ancient Rome allowed unilateral no-fault divorce as early as the 2nd century BC, making it one of the earliest legal systems to let either spouse end a marriage without proving wrongdoing — a right many modern legal systems didn't grant until the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 他的前妻带着孩子搬到了外地。
examples.pinyin: Tā de qiánqī dài zhe háizi bān dào le wàidì.
examples.english: His ex-wife moved to another city with the child.

examples.hanzi: 他很少提起自己的前妻。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn shǎo tíqǐ zìjǐ de qiánqī.
examples.english: He rarely mentions his ex-wife.

components.note: 夫 (man) — the main part. Dictionary reading: something 丿 slipping from a hand. Memory aid: a man 夫 dropping what he held — 失去 to lose.
攵 (tap, hand with stick) — striking or acting on something: 放, 改, 政, 教; in 败 a blow breaking a cowry 贝 shell (valuable): ruin, defeat.
贝 (bèi) is a loose sound hint for bài.
者 (zhě) is a sound clue for 都 dū, 著 zhù, 煮 zhǔ, 猪 zhū and 诸 zhū; as a word it means "one who", as in 作者 author.

example.hanzi: 没有人愿意被称为失败者。
example.pinyin: méiyǒu rén yuànyì bèi chēng wéi shībàizhě.
example.english: No one wants to be called a loser.
example.fact: Wilbur and Orville Wright endured years of crashes and failed glider tests at Kitty Hawk before their December 1903 flight lasted just 12 seconds — yet it became the first sustained, controlled, powered flight in human history.

examples.hanzi: 别把一次失败看成失败者的标志。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ yí cì shībài kàn chéng shībàizhě de biāozhì.
examples.english: Don't treat one failure as the mark of a loser.

examples.hanzi: 比赛里总有赢家，也有失败者。
examples.pinyin: Bǐsài lǐ zǒngyǒu yíngjiā, yě yǒu shībàizhě.
examples.english: In every competition there are winners and also losers.

components.note: 耂 (old) — shown in 老 old and 者; 考 first meant an aged person (the same word as 老), then to examine.
丂 (kǎo) gives the sound; also in 巧 qiǎo, 烤 kǎo and 拷 kǎo.
马 (horse) — horses: 骑, 驾, 骄; 验 first meant testing a horse, then any test.
佥 (qiān) gives the -ian rhyme; same part in 险 xiǎn, 检 jiǎn, 脸 liǎn, 签 qiān.

example.hanzi: 这场比赛是对他体力的一次考验。
example.pinyin: zhè chǎng bǐsài shì duì tā tǐlì de yī cì kǎoyàn.
example.english: This competition is a test of his physical strength.
example.fact: NASA astronaut candidates undergo a water-survival test where they're strapped into a mock capsule and dropped into a pool, then must escape while inverted and disoriented — an ordeal deliberately designed to simulate emergency splashdown conditions.

examples.hanzi: 这次考试是对我们的考验。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì shì duì wǒmen de kǎoyàn.
examples.english: This exam is a test for us.

examples.hanzi: 时间会考验朋友之间的感情。
examples.pinyin: Shíjiān huì kǎoyàn péngyou zhījiān de gǎnqíng.
examples.english: Time will test the friendship between friends.

components.note: 罒 (net, form of 网) — nets and entrapment: 罗 net, 罚 punish, 骂 scold; here a net of wrongdoing 非 catching the guilty.
非 (not, wrong) — what is wrong or unlawful; in 罪 it is the wrongdoing caught in the net.
彳 (step) — left half of a crossroads: 行 pictures a crossroads, so to go, and (háng) a row or trade.

example.hanzi: 法庭正在审理他的罪行。
example.pinyin: fǎtíng zhèngzài shěnlǐ tā de zuìxíng.
example.english: The court is currently trying his offense.
example.fact: The Nuremberg trials of 1945-46 were the first international tribunals to prosecute leaders for war crimes and crimes against humanity, establishing legal precedents — like rejecting 'just following orders' as a defense — that still shape international criminal law today.

examples.hanzi: 他承认了自己的全部罪行。
examples.pinyin: Tā chéngrèn le zìjǐ de quánbù zuìxíng.
examples.english: He admitted all of his crimes.

examples.hanzi: 法官宣布了他的罪行。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān xuānbù le tā de zuìxíng.
examples.english: The judge announced his offenses.

components.note: 攵 (tap, strike) — 攵 marks an action, as in 教, 放, 收; 效 is to imitate or produce results.
交 (jiāo) — near sound — 效 is xiào; 交 also sounds out 校 xiào and 较 jiào.
力 (strength) — marks effort and work, as in 动 move, 努 strive, 办; 劳 is toil, labour.

example.hanzi: 他愿意为公司效劳多年。
example.pinyin: tā yuànyì wèi gōngsī xiàoláo duō nián.
example.english: He is willing to serve the company for many years.
example.fact: Honeybee workers spend their roughly six-week lifespan working themselves to death for the colony — foraging bees fly up to 800 kilometers over their lifetime and can visit over 2,000 flowers in a single day of gathering for the hive.

examples.hanzi: 有什么需要我效劳的吗？
examples.pinyin: Yǒu shénme xūyào wǒ xiàoláo de ma?
examples.english: Is there anything I can do for you?

examples.hanzi: 我愿意为您效劳。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yuànyì wèi nín xiàoláo.
examples.english: I'm happy to be of service to you.

components.note: 日 (sun) — day and time, as in 晴 clear, 早 early, 明 bright; time was read from the sun.
寸 (cùn) stands in for 寺 sì in the traditional 時; sound clue is loose. 寺 also gives 诗 shī and 持 chí.
衣 (clothing) — clothes and wear: 衬, 被, 袋; 装 is dress, then to pretend or to load.
壮 (zhuàng) is a near sound match for zhuāng; also in 状 zhuàng and 妆 zhuāng.

example.hanzi: 巴黎每年都会举办著名的时装秀。
example.pinyin: bālí měi nián dōu huì jǔbàn zhùmíng de shízhuāng xiù.
example.english: Paris holds a famous fashion show every year.
example.fact: Paris Fashion Week traces its roots to the Chambre Syndicale de la Couture Parisienne, founded in 1868, making it one of the oldest continuously running fashion institutions in the world — over 150 years before today's livestreamed runway shows.

examples.hanzi: 这件时装很适合春天穿。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shízhuāng hěn shìhé chūntiān chuān.
examples.english: This outfit is very suitable for wearing in spring.

examples.hanzi: 她在一家时装店工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài yì jiā shízhuāng diàn gōngzuò.
examples.english: She works at a fashion store.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 稍 first meant the tip of the grain, a little bit.
肖 (xiāo) — near sound — 稍 is shāo; 肖 also sounds out 消 xiāo and 削 xiāo.
后 (after, behind) — two words merged in simplified writing: old 后 "ruler" (皇后 empress) and 後 "behind, later" (as in 然后).

example.hanzi: 会议稍后开始,请大家先坐好。
example.pinyin: huìyì shāohòu kāishǐ, qǐng dàjiā xiān zuò hǎo.
example.english: The meeting will start shortly; everyone please take a seat first.
example.fact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth, so whenever you look at the Sun, you're actually seeing it as it appeared slightly earlier — if it suddenly vanished, we wouldn't know for over eight minutes.

examples.hanzi: 我稍后给你回电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shāohòu gěi nǐ huí diànhuà.
examples.english: I'll call you back a little later.

examples.hanzi: 稍后我们会把资料发给您。
examples.pinyin: Shāohòu wǒmen huì bǎ zīliào fā gěi nín.
examples.english: We'll send you the materials shortly.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — marks actions done by hand, as in 拿, 提, 抬; 搬 is to move things.
般 (bān) gives the sound exactly: 搬 bān.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 室 room, 安 safe, 字 character; 家 is home.
豕 (pig) — a pig under a roof: pigs were kept in the home, hence home and family.

example.hanzi: 我们下个月要搬家到另一个城市。
example.pinyin: wǒmen xià gè yuè yào bānjiā dào lìng yī gè chéngshì.
example.english: We're moving to another city next month.
example.fact: According to US Census data, the average American moves about 11.7 times in their lifetime, a notably higher rate of internal migration than in most other developed nations, largely driven by job mobility.

examples.hanzi: 我们家上个月刚搬家。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā shàng ge yuè gāng bānjiā.
examples.english: Our family just moved house last month.

examples.hanzi: 搬家的时候，朋友来帮了忙。
examples.pinyin: Bānjiā de shíhou, péngyou lái bāng le máng.
examples.english: My friends came to help when we were moving.

meanings: to host (a TV or radio program etc)

components.note: 主 (master, host) — a lamp with a flame on top; a lamp stand was the centre of the room. 主 also sounds out 注 zhù, 住 zhù and 柱 zhù.
扌 (hand) — hand actions, as in 打, 拿, 抱: holding on.
寺 (sì) is a loose sound clue for chí; 寺 also in 诗 shī, 待 dài, 特 tè and 等 děng.

example.hanzi: 她将主持今晚的颁奖典礼。
example.pinyin: tā jiāng zhǔchí jīnwǎn de bānjiǎng diǎnlǐ.
example.english: She will host tonight's award ceremony.
example.fact: The Academy Awards ceremony has aired live on television since 1953, and its unscripted hosting segments are considered so unpredictable that producers build in extensive contingency plans, including backup hosts kept on standby in case of an emergency.

examples.hanzi: 老师主持了今天的班会。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī zhǔchí le jīntiān de bānhuì.
examples.english: The teacher chaired today's class meeting.

examples.hanzi: 他主持这个节目已经十年了。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǔchí zhège jiémù yǐjīng shí nián le.
examples.english: He has hosted this program for ten years.

components.note: 田 (field) — a field above 力 (strength): a man is one who works the fields with strength.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 一名男子在公园里跑步锻炼。
example.pinyin: yī míng nánzǐ zài gōngyuán lǐ pǎobù duànliàn.
example.english: A man was running and exercising in the park.
example.fact: The men's 100-meter world record, held by Usain Bolt at 9.58 seconds since 2009, requires reaching speeds of over 44 km/h at peak stride — faster than many dog breeds can sustain over the same short distance.

examples.hanzi: 一名男子在车站等人。
examples.pinyin: Yì míng nánzǐ zài chēzhàn děng rén.
examples.english: A man is waiting for someone at the station.

examples.hanzi: 那位男子手里拿着一束花。
examples.pinyin: Nà wèi nánzǐ shǒu lǐ ná zhe yí shù huā.
examples.english: That man is holding a bouquet of flowers in his hand.
